summary: Answered your three notes: every Short's description and hashtags now name its famous subject (Elon Musk) even with a plain title, and a new impact report tracks whether the channel is actually improving. Extended one experiment; the other four wait for data.
why: Owner notes come first. The evaluator asked to extend ending-beats-act-and-vary (2 vs 3 videos, no clear effect); nothing else matured, and 5 experiments run (the cap).

findings.title: Is the channel improving? Partly
findings.detail: Shorts by week (late Oct -> 2 Nov week): % viewed 39.7% -> 54.6%, average view 17.9 -> 23.2 s, but stayed-to-watch flat at ~39% (6 in 10 swipe away at the start) and median 48 h views 211 -> 43. Retention fixes worked; the first second is now the bottleneck.

findings.title: Variant system
findings.detail: Defaults 20-27 s (908 median vs 133), secret hook (708), plain title (460 vs 140, only 4 videos, confounded with length).

findings.title: Best formats by 48 h views
findings.detail: how_they_make_money 9.77x (n 5), money_scale 2.33x, secret_of_rich 2.06x and 68.5% viewed; rule_change 0.36x but 42.0% viewed, not retired.

findings.title: Experiments
findings.detail: ending-beats-act-and-vary extended to 21 days; hook-voice-matches-frame day 21 of 28; you-in-the-core-story 1 of 4; quiet-bed 1 of 4 and chart-gap-fill 2 of 4 long videos per arm.

changes.title: Subject named in description and hashtag
changes.detail: Plans carry `subject`; check-plan fails a Short whose description's first two lines or hashtags don't name it (generator/formats.py, planner.md, test).

changes.title: Impact report
changes.detail: python -m generator.impact writes improvement/weekly/impact.json: Shorts per week (views, % viewed, stayed to watch, view seconds) and each landed change's 14 days before/after.
